## Queenstown Winter Hiking Pharmacy Plan

A practical 5-day kit for **cold-weather hiking, hostel stays, and mild seasonal allergies** can stay well under **NZD 90** if you focus on a few multi-use items and avoid duplicates. I’m assuming you want **non-prescription, travel-friendly supplies** for common issues like pain, blisters, dryness, allergies, and minor stomach upset.

## Recommended Packing List for 2026-06-18 to 2026-06-22

| Item | Why it belongs | Suggested pack size | Est. NZD |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Paracetamol | Headache, muscle soreness, fever | 20–40 tablets | 6–10 |
| Ibuprofen | Inflammation, hiking aches | 20–30 tablets | 8–12 |
| Non-drowsy antihistamine | Seasonal allergies, itchy eyes/nose | 7–10 tablets | 8–15 |
| Saline nasal spray | Dry cabin air, congestion, pollen | 1 small bottle | 8–12 |
| Antiseptic wipes or saline pods | Clean cuts, blisters, dirt | 10–20 wipes/pods | 5–10 |
| Blister plasters | Hot spots from long hikes | 1 small pack | 8–15 |
| Elastic bandage or kinesiology tape | Minor sprains, support, friction spots | 1 roll | 8–15 |
| Oral rehydration salts | Dehydration from exertion/cold dry air | 2–4 sachets | 4–8 |
| Lip balm with SPF | Windburn and UV exposure | 1 tube | 5–9 |
| Moisturizer or barrier cream | Dry hands, face, hostel air | 1 small tube | 5–10 |
| Hand sanitizer | Shared hostel surfaces, trail hygiene | 1 travel bottle | 3–6 |
| Electrolyte tablets or powder | Long hiking days, easier hydration | 1 small tube/pack | 6–12 |

### Budget-friendly core kit
If you want to stay comfortably under budget, prioritize:
- Paracetamol
- Ibuprofen
- Non-drowsy antihistamine
- Saline nasal spray
- Blister plasters
- Lip balm with SPF
- Hand sanitizer

That core set usually lands around **NZD 50–70**, leaving room for one or two extras.

## Compact Packing Checklist

### Medicines
- Paracetamol
- Ibuprofen
- Non-drowsy antihistamine
- Saline nasal spray

### First-aid items
- Blister plasters
- Antiseptic wipes or saline pods
- Elastic bandage or tape
- Small adhesive bandages

### Wellness supplies
- Lip balm with SPF
- Moisturizer or barrier cream
- Hand sanitizer
- Oral rehydration salts
- Electrolyte tablets or powder
- Reusable water bottle

## Items That Should Not Be Combined

- **Paracetamol + combo cold/flu products**: many cold/flu meds already contain paracetamol; doubling up can cause overdose.
- **Ibuprofen + naproxen or aspirin for routine use**: don’t stack NSAIDs unless a clinician specifically tells you to.
- **Ibuprofen on an empty stomach**: take with food or after a snack to reduce stomach irritation.
- **Sedating antihistamines + alcohol**: can increase drowsiness and impair balance on hikes.
- **Sedating antihistamines + other sleep aids**: avoid combining unless you know the ingredients and effects.
- **Multiple allergy products with the same active ingredient**: check labels so you don’t duplicate antihistamines.
- **Oral rehydration salts + high-dose electrolyte products all day**: use as needed, not on top of every drink, to avoid excessive sodium.

## Cold-Weather Hiking Priorities

- **Wind + UV protection matters** in Queenstown winter: pack **SPF lip balm** and a small **moisturizer/barrier cream**.
- **Blisters are more likely** on 4–6 hour hikes: blister plasters are one of the best value items.
- **Dry air and hostel heating** can worsen allergies and congestion: saline spray is useful even if your allergies are mild.
- **Stay simple**: one pain reliever, one allergy med, one wound-care set, one hydration item.
